target_customer: Consumers and online video viewers who wanted to clip, annotate, comment on and share video from any site
problem: Online video could not easily be excerpted, annotated or synced with slides. Omnisio let users mark up and stitch clips from across the web.
business_model: free consumer web service with planned advertising

founders.name: Ryan Junee
founders.background_notes: No bio on the YC page.

founders.name: Simon Ratner
founders.background_notes: No bio on the YC page.

founders.name: Julian Frumar
previous_startups: Omnisio (acquired by Google); self-described as 2x YC technical founder
founders.background_notes: YC page bio: frontend and zero-to-one product design and development.

technical_complexity.rationale: Time-based annotation and clip stitching across third-party video hosts and slide syncing required standard but non-trivial web engineering in 2008.

defensibility.rationale: The feature set was easy to copy, and YouTube already ran its own beta annotation tool that Omnisio's software was expected to replace.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: YouTube acquired Omnisio in late July 2008, announced on the YouTube blog; the site stopped taking new users and redirected to YouTube, and the founders joined to build features there.

market_need_then: Online video was booming in 2008 and users lacked ways to excerpt and comment inside videos; the YouTube video team saw value in the annotation technology enough to buy it.

identity.logo: not described by any source found

brand_strength.rationale: No source shows press about the brand, a community, or lasting recognition; the brand ended within months of the acquisition.

outcome_analysis: Omnisio launched in the YC Winter 2008 batch and drew press for its clip and annotation tools, then sold to YouTube in July 2008 within months of public launch. The deal was a team and technology purchase aimed at YouTube's annotation tools, the price is disputed (one Polish report cited a TechCrunch figure of 15 million, others say undisclosed), and the standalone product was folded into YouTube.
notes: Company site returned HTTP 503 so it was not read. No funding found; searches returned unrelated companies. Price unverified (15M claim from one secondary report, others undisclosed). YC page names Google in its header and YouTube in the body. No dated competitor sources found, so the list is empty.
